title: One-hour high-sensitivity troponin rule-out in a district hospital chest pain unit: a rapid review
subtitle: Rapid review for the hospital quality committee, 2 December 2026
statement: The chest pain unit rules out myocardial infarction with troponin samples at presentation and three hours, and ruled-out patients spend a median of seven hours in the department. Consultants propose a one-hour rule-out pathway. The quality committee needs a rapid review of how safe one-hour rule-out is at 30 days, how many patients it rules out, how much time it saves, and what fails in practice, with particular attention to older patients and people with kidney disease.
whoAffected: About 9,000 adults a year with suspected acute coronary syndrome at a 550-bed district general hospital, 38 percent of them aged 75 or over; emergency and cardiology staff; the laboratory; and the quality committee that must approve the change.
whatHurts: Long waits for a second sample crowd the unit and delay care for other patients; a faster pathway that missed myocardial infarctions, or that ruled out few of the older patients who make up much of the workload, would add risk without the promised relief.
currentPractice: High-sensitivity troponin I at presentation and at three hours; discharge after two results below the threshold; median seven hours in the department for ruled-out patients.
whyNow: The unit is full most afternoons, consultants have proposed the change, and the committee meets on 2 December 2026.
patientCenteredGoal: Patients without a heart attack go home sooner and safely, and patients who have one are not sent home.
summary: Problem framed as a rapid review of safety, rule-out yield, time saved and practical failure points of a one-hour pathway.
